tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- Recorded session shows the admin flow: open order view for an existing order_id, click Reorder, reach sales_order_create page prefilled with customer/items, then click Submit Order and receive a success message and new order view. The tool will reproduce these deterministic steps.

Task Definition:
- Single purpose: create a new order in Magento admin by reordering an existing order identified by order_id. The tool will navigate to the order view, trigger Reorder, submit the created order, and return the new order number and confirmation.

Action Plan (detailed):
1) Navigate to {base_admin_url}/sales_order/view/order_id/{order_id}/ to open the order view.
2) Verify the order view loaded (extract page content) and ensure 'Reorder' control exists.
3) Click the Reorder button/link using a visible-text or href-based XPath (robust across admin themes).
4) Wait briefly for the Create New Order page to load and extract page content to confirm prefilled items/customer.
5) Click the Submit Order control. Use an XPath that matches input[type=submit] (value/title) or button text.
6) Wait for server processing/redirect.
7) Extract confirmation page content and return the new order number and the confirmation message.

Variable Identification (tool inputs):
- base_admin_url (required): The admin base URL. Use exactly as recorded (including protocol and admin frontName). This lets the tool construct all admin URLs deterministically.
- order_id (required): The internal order id used in the admin URL. This is the dynamic value that chooses which existing order to copy.

Step Optimization / Selector strategy:
- Prefer direct URL navigation to open the order view (deterministic) rather than navigating through the Orders grid; the session includes direct view URLs.
- Prefer text-based XPath selectors for 'Reorder' and 'Submit Order' to be robust across Magento admin skins and differing element types (<button>, <input>, <a>). Examples used: //button[normalize-space(.)='Reorder'] and //input[@type='submit' and (@value='Submit Order' or @title='Submit Order')] | //button[normalize-space(.)='Submit Order'].
- Avoid relying on guessed or environment-specific ids; if a specific id/title is present at runtime, the automation engine should prefer it. The tool returns page extracts so the caller can validate and switch to a stronger selector if necessary.
- Insert short waits after critical clicks to allow navigation/AJAX to complete. The recorded session showed navigation and success messages often appear after a short delay.

Assumptions and constraints:
- The recorded actions included a login step; per instructions the tool assumes the session is already authenticated in the browser context used to execute these steps (do NOT include authentication in the tool). If the session is not authenticated, the navigation will show the admin login page and the tool will not complete.
- The admin UI can render buttons as <button>, <input type='submit'> or anchors. XPaths cover these cases.
- JavaScript-driven modals and AJAX are present on the Create New Order page; waits are included but automation should handle waiting for the page to become ready/visible before clicks.
- Final save action is performed by clicking the 'Submit Order' control in the UI rather than attempting to call inferred POST endpoints directly (more robust with CSRF/form keys and sessions).

Deterministic behavior and minimal steps:
- Steps are strictly sequential and deterministic: navigation (direct URL) → click Reorder → confirm create page → click Submit Order → extract created order.
- No optional branching or extra filters are included; only essential steps to accomplish the single task are present.

Outputs and verification:
- The tool will produce the extracted 'created_order' page content which must include the success message and the new order number (e.g., 'Order # 145000027'). The caller can parse the 'created_order' output to confirm success.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- If the session is not authenticated, the initial navigation will reach the login page. The tool purposely omits authentication; callers must ensure an authenticated admin context.
- If the Reorder or Submit Order elements are not present or have different labels in a localized admin, the tool will return the extracted pages so the caller can inspect and adjust selectors. Consider using title/value attributes where known.

Overall: This tool reproduces the recorded admin Reorder flow in a compact, repeatable sequence and exposes robust, text-based XPaths as default selectors while returning page content for final verification or selector tuning.
name: magento_admin_reorder_from_existing_order
description: Create a new admin order by reordering an existing order (uses Magento admin Reorder → Submit Order flow). Navigates to the order view for a given order_id, clicks Reorder, and clicks Submit Order. Returns the new order number and confirmation message.

steps.description: Open the existing order view in the admin for the provided order_id.
Capture page text and links to verify we are on the order view and to collect any visible confirmation text or links.
steps.goal: Confirm the order view loaded, extract order header and ensure a Reorder control is present (look for 'Order #' header and Reorder button).

steps.description: Click the Reorder action on the order view. Uses text-based XPath and href-based fallback to be robust across admin themes.
Allow navigation/AJAX to complete and the Create New Order page to load after clicking Reorder.
Validate that the Reorder action opened the Create New Order screen and capture fields/totals for diagnosis.
steps.goal: Confirm the create-order page loaded and capture order-create page indicators (items, customer name, totals).

steps.description: Click the 'Submit Order' control. XPath covers both input[type=submit] and button variants and matches value/title/visible text.
steps.xpath: //input[@type='submit' and (normalize-space(@value)='Submit Order' or normalize-space(@title)='Submit Order')] | //button[normalize-space(.)='Submit Order']

steps.description: Wait for the submission to be processed and for the admin to redirect to the new order view / confirmation page.
Capture the success message (e.g., 'The order has been created.') and the order header 'Order # {NEW_ORDER}' to return as the tool output.
steps.goal: Extract the confirmation message and the newly created order number and view URL.

input_schema.name: base_admin_url
input_schema.description: Base admin URL including protocol and admin frontName (example: "http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin"). Do not include a trailing slash.

input_schema.name: order_id
input_schema.description: Internal order id used in admin URLs (the numeric id used in the view URL, e.g. '204'). This will be used to open: {base_admin_url}/sales_order/view/order_id/{order_id}/
